nodes.title: Text Bridge Node
widgets_values:
### 🔗 Text Bridge Node — Function & Usage

The **Text Bridge** node is a utility for managing and editing prompt text within your ComfyUI workflow. It offers two flexible behaviors:

---

### 1. 🚦 Pass-Through Mode  
- **Leave the field empty** to simply pass the input prompt through unchanged.
- Useful when you want to forward a prompt from an earlier node without modification.

### 2. ✍️ Override Mode  
- **Enter or paste a custom prompt** in the text field to override the pass-through.
- This lets you quickly edit, customize, or replace the prompt at this point in your workflow.

---

> 💡 **Tip:**  
> Use the Text Bridge node to conveniently switch between using upstream prompts and custom instructions—no need to rewire your workflow!

nodes.title: Settings
widgets_values:
## 🧠 Text, Image or Style — Node Settings

This node lets you choose how the image is generated based on different input types:

- **`setting_1` – Text to Image**  
  Input a plain text description. The LLM will generate a compatible prompt and summary to create a new image.

- **`setting_2` – Inspired by Reference**  
  Upload a reference image. The AI generates a new image inspired by its composition, layout, or mood. This is useful when you want variation while keeping the essence of the reference.

- **`setting_3` – Style Image to Image**  
  Apply a new style to an existing image. You can restyle the whole image or just the subject (e.g., change style while keeping the pose and structure).

---

## 🧽 Style Denoise: Low, Medium, High

- **Low** – Keeps the original image mostly unchanged. Good for subtle style overlays.
- **Medium** – A balanced transformation.
- **High** – Strongly applies the style, modifying the image significantly.

> 🎯 Tip: Use **Low** when preserving the subject or composition is important.

---

## 🌀 Perturbation Pipeline

Perturbation introduces micro-level noise and irregularities to help:

- Break uniformity in AI-generated surfaces
- Add texture and pixel-level realism
- Simulate photographic grain or painted roughness

> ✨ Great for making AI images feel more organic and less digital.

---

## 🩹 InPaint

Enable this to selectively modify areas of an image:

- Works with masks to edit only the selected area
- Keeps the rest of the image untouched

---

nodes.title: Pre Upscale Perturbation Setting
widgets_values:
### 🔧 Perturbation & Film Grain Tips

**🌀 Perturbation Texture Strength**  
- Recommended range: **25–50**
- If you notice **artifacts during upscaling**, reduce to **25**
- For clean yet detailed textures, **50** works best

---

**🎞️ Film Grain**  
- Works **best at this stage** of processing  
- Adds subtle realism and depth  
- ✅ Recommended: **Enable it** for a natural finish  
- 🧪 Feel free to **experiment** with different grain intensities for creative results

---

> 🎯 **Tip:** If using aggressive upscalers or denoisers, lower perturbation and grain may preserve clarity better.

nodes.title: Pre Final Upscale Perturbation Setting
widgets_values:
### 🎯 Perturbation Texture Usage Guide (Second Upscale Stage)

**📍 Strength Recommendation:**
- For second upscale or pre-final render:  
  Set **Perturbation Texture Strength between 10–50**
- 🧩 **Default setting:** `Natural` texture type at **strength 10**

---

**🎛️ Texture Type Options (in Custom Node):**

| Option          | Best Used For                                              |
|------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Natural**       | Balanced, organic texture — ideal for stylized portraits or general image enhancement without overwhelming details |
| **Film Grain**    | Adds cinematic noise — great for final renders or creative film looks |
| **Skin Pore**     | Subtle realism — best for **close-ups** or portraits needing natural facial texture |
| **Fine Detail**   | Emphasizes high-frequency textures — perfect for mechanical, fabric, or intricate object renders |

---

> 🧪 **Tip:** Use lower strength (10–25) for subtle texture and higher (30–50) for more pronounced detail. Adjust based on subject complexity and desired finish.

nodes.title: Target Style
widgets_values:
### 🎨 Style Transformation Tips

**🛠️ Target Style** can be used to change the **entire theme** of the image or **specific subject elements**.

- **🔁 High Denoise**: Best for **full style change** while preserving overall composition.
- **🎯 Medium / Low Denoise**: Ideal for **minor tweaks** or **specific subject/object style changes** with better consistency.

---

#### ✏️ Some Style Examples *(Medium or High Denoise)*:

- Anime Style  
- Ghibli Style  
- Flat Vector Style  
- Pixel Art Style  
- Illustration Style  
- Disney Pixar Style  

---

#### 🧠 Go Creative *(High Denoise)*:

- Robotic Cat in Toxic Green Water  
- Cat made out of Yarn, Cinematic  
- Cat made out of Swarovski Crystals  
- Cat made out of Paper, 3D Render  

---

#### 👁️ Specific Element Tweaks *(Low Denoise)*:

- Psychedelic Eye Colors  

---

> 💡 **Tip:** Start small with low denoise for subtle effects. Increase denoise to amplify stylization and transformation.

nodes.title: InPainting Changes
widgets_values:
### 🖌️ Inpainting Instructions Guide

**📍 How It Works:**
- You must **load a mask** that defines the area to be inpainted.
- The model will modify **only the masked area** while preserving the rest of the image.

---

**✏️ What You Can Do in the Mask Area:**

Use natural language instructions to perform tasks like:

**Change subjects:**

  - `Change cat to frog`  
  - `Change the boy to father`

**Alter surrounding elements:**
  - `Change the fishes to sharks`  
  - `Change the water to swamp-like muddle brown`

**Add / Remove components:**
  - `Add a hat to the girl`  
  - `Remove the tree in the background`

> 💡 **Tip:** You only need to describe the change. The LLM will automatically preserve the style, lighting, and composition.

nodes.title: Text LLM
widgets_values: You are a prompt enrichment model. Given a creative or abstract text prompt, expand it into a vivid, richly detailed description suitable for language models like T5XXL and LLaMA. Preserve the original theme, but enhance it with sensory details, spatial relationships, and evocative language. Output a natural-sounding, immersive prompt of 1–2 sentences. Respond in a single continuous paragraph. Avoid any kind of structured formatting, such as bullet points, numbered lists, headings, bolded sections, or labeled parts. Do not divide the output into categories—write as one seamless descriptive passage.
A vector of a kid in a superhero suit

nodes.title: Image LLM
widgets_values:
You are a professional visual description model. Given an input image, generate only a detailed prompt-style description. Do not mention that it is an image. Do not include any explanation, interpretation, or preface like “this image shows.” Simply describe the visual content with rich detail that could be used as a generation prompt for an AI model. Stay factual, use a neutral tone, and avoid fictional or imaginative content unless explicitly visible.

Respond in a single continuous paragraph using natural language. Avoid any kind of structured formatting, such as bullet points, numbered lists, headings, bolded sections, or labeled parts. Do not divide the output into categories—write as one seamless descriptive passage. Limit to 3-4 descriptive sentences.
Describe the image. Ouput description only as a prompt.

You are a prompt modification assistant for inpainting tasks.

You will receive a detailed base prompt describing the entire image, along with a free-text "Changes:" instruction from the user.

Your task is to modify only the portion of the prompt affected by the requested change, while preserving all unrelated details exactly as written.

Do not rewrite or paraphrase the entire prompt.

Modify only what is necessary to apply the change accurately and naturally.

Maintain all visual characteristics such as composition, lighting, spatial layout, and descriptive tone unless directly impacted by the change.

When replacing a subject, remove or adapt any descriptors that are no longer applicable to the new subject.

Ensure the revised prompt reads fluently and maintains internal consistency.

Changes: Change cat to frog

nodes.title: LLM Summary
widgets_values: You are a prompt compression model. Given a richly detailed text description, rewrite it into a short, visually descriptive prompt optimized for CLIP-based models. Dynamically preserve any stylistic or artistic cues present in the original text. Focus only on concrete visual elements such as objects, colors, materials, textures, lighting, and spatial layout. Avoid emotions, storytelling, or abstract language. Keep the output literal, compact, and under 25 words.
Describe the image. Ouput description only as a prompt.

Describe the image as if it were created in the Target Style as a prompt. Maintain all visible subjects, layout, and spatial relationships exactly as seen. Use image-generation–friendly language that reflects the Target Style’s texture, color treatment, lighting, brushwork, and detail level. Capture all key visual elements: facial features, expressions, pose, clothing, accessories, background, and environment. Do not add or remove objects. Avoid poetic or figurative language. Limit to 4–5 descriptive sentences.

Target Style: Psychedelic Colored Eyes
